rulings: Task 5: Ruling: keep preferred-port and valid warm-hint priority, but select the first verified owner among remaining ports by response arrival, as P5 specifies — the old changed-port-set test assumed ordered selection between two fixtures serving the same PID. Its replacement asserts both valid owner URLs and proves preferred probing after invalidation; PID/profile safety stays tested. Cost if wrong: configurations exposing one owned PID through several nonpreferred servers can select a different equally owned URL.

Task 6: Ruling: reject the GraphQL projection and retain REST+ETag, the negative selection outcome explicitly required by P6 when parity/benefit fail — live all-affiliation query returns61 vs REST60, either default affiliation returns55/misses5; REST remains304 after each query. No production GraphQL path/parser is introduced, so its proposed mock DTO/cursor tests are inapplicable; real failed parity is the gate evidence. Cost if wrong: a future, different projection may offer cold-body savings but is not enabled now.

Task 7: Ruling: verify the frozen full suite in six disjoint sequential manifests through the unchanged 3-worker/15-minute Node runner with renderer enabled — the prior release single full run exceeded900000ms. Final: Ruling: declined universal OAuth team/archive/cursor parity is not an adoption claim — no GraphQL product catalog is shipped; the existing OAuth-only REST contract remains. Cost if wrong: potential cold projection savings remain unavailable until a distinct compatible route is proven.

Final: Ruling: controlled service measurements prove payload and scheduling/response-size changes, not universal live GitHub latency or UI paint — only P6 is a live network experiment, with seven samples. Cost if wrong: users may not observe a visible speed change in their environment; no broad latency guarantee is made.
